'''Craig Jon Hawker''' (born 11 January 1964) is an Australian-born chemist. His research has focused on the interface between [[Organic chemistry|organic]] and [[polymer chemistry]], with emphasis on the design, synthesis, and application of well-defined macromolecular structures in [[biotechnology]], [[microelectronics]], and [[surface science]]. Hawker holds more than 45 U.S. [[patents]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Patents by Inventor Craig J. Hawker |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/craig-j-hawker |website=Justia Patents |publisher=Justia |access-date=26 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306042627/https://patents.justia.com/inventor/craig-j-hawker |url-status=live }}</ref> and he has co-authored over 300 papers in the areas of [[nanotechnology]], [[materials science]], and [[chemistry]]. He was listed as one of the top 100 most cited chemists worldwide over the decade 1992–2002,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hirsch index ranks top chemists.|url=http://www.rsc.org/chemistryworld/news/2007/april/23040701.asp|access-date=18 January 2011|archive-date=7 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607185021/http://www.rsc.org/chemistryworld/News/2007/April/23040701.asp|url-status=live}}</ref> and again in 2000–2010.<ref>{{cite web |title=TOP 100 CHEMISTS, 2000-2010 |url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/dr/sci/misc/Top100Chemists2000-10/ |publisher=Clarivate Analytics |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=29 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229140346/http://archive.sciencewatch.com/dr/sci/misc/Top100Chemists2000-10/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2021, Hawker was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for contributions to polymer chemistry through synthetic organic chemistry concepts and the advancement of molecular engineering principles. He is the director of the California Nanosystems Institute and holds a number of other laboratory directorships at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].

He was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2022-nas-election.html | title=2022 NAS Election | access-date=12 March 2023 | archive-date=10 May 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220510102559/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2022-nas-election.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Education==
Hawker was born in [[Australia]] and attended high school in [[Queensland]]. It was in high school that he developed his interest in chemistry because, as he put it, "it really allowed me to develop things with my hands. Chemistry is a very hands-on science."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ober |first1=Christopher |title=Interview with Craig Hawker (YouTube) |agency=Materials Research Laboratory |publisher=University of California, Santa Barbara |date=7 February 2011}}</ref> He studied at the [[University of Queensland]] and graduated with a Chemistry degree.<ref>{{cite web |title=Craig J. Hawker: Biography |url=http://hawkergroup.mrl.ucsb.edu/craig-j-hawker |website=Hawker Group |publisher=University of California, Santa Barbara |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=21 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190221015323/http://hawkergroup.mrl.ucsb.edu/craig-j-hawker |url-status=live }}</ref> He worked with Professor [[Alan R. Battersby]] at [[Cambridge University]] on his post-graduate studies achieving his PhD in bio-organic chemistry.<ref>{{cite web |title=Executive Profile: Craig J. Hawker |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=49647858&privcapId=254955910 |website=Company Overview of Tricida |publisher=Bloomberg |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306043742/https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=49647858&privcapId=254955910 |url-status=live }}</ref> Hawker then moved to the United States to pursue post-graduate work at [[Cornell University]] in 1988.<ref>{{cite web |title=Craig Hawker |url=http://www.cns.ucsb.edu/people/craig-hawker-0.html |website=Center for Nanotechnology in Society |publisher=University of California Center for Nanotechnology in Society |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044230/http://www.cns.ucsb.edu/people/craig-hawker-0.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Research history==
[[File:California NanoSystems Institute (CNSI) building with mural at the University of California, Santa Barbara, Goleta, California LCCN2013632013.tif|thumb|The California NanoSystems Institute building with mural at the University of California, Santa Barbara]]
In 1990, Hawker returned to Queensland as a Queen Elizabeth II Research fellow at the University of Queensland.<ref>{{cite web |title=Craig J. Hawker |url=https://acscerm2019.org/keynotes/hawker/ |website=ACS: Chemistry for Life |publisher=Australian Chemical Society |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306043933/https://acscerm2019.org/keynotes/hawker/ |url-status=live }}</ref> From 2004, he was a research staff member at the [[IBM Almaden Research Center]] in California.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Craig Hawker Director, California Nanosystems Institute University of California, Santa Barbara |url=https://www.cbns.org.au/profiles/professor-craig-hawker/ |website=ARC Centre of Excellence Convergent and Bio-Nano Science and Technology |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044550/https://www.cbns.org.au/profiles/professor-craig-hawker/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Hawker is the director of the [[California NanoSystems Institute]], co-director of the Materials Research Laboratory, and the Alan and Ruth Heeger Professor of Interdisciplinary Science at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Craig Hawker |url=http://www.chem.ucsb.edu/people/craig-hawker |website=UC Santa Barbara: Chemistry and Biology |publisher=University of California, Santa Barbara |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=21 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190221015248/http://www.chem.ucsb.edu/people/craig-hawker |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Influence and research focus==
In 2012, Hawker won the [[Centenary Prize]] from the [[Royal Society]] for developing strategies for the design of new [[polymers]], which has had a major influence in the area and on those studying polymers.<ref>{{cite web |title=UC Santa Barbara's Craig Hawker wins Centenary Prize for Chemistry |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2012-05/uoc--usb051612.php |website=EurekaAlert! |publisher=AAAS |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306043749/https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2012-05/uoc--usb051612.php |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2013, Hawker and another colleague invented [[Olaplex]], a successful commercial product designed to relink hair bonds and to help reduce hair breakage.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nhung |first1=Nguyen |title=Olaplex: The Science Behind the Strand |date=April 2015 |url=https://archesnews.com/olaplex-the-science-behind-the-strand/ |publisher=Arches |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=30 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190130230112/http://archesnews.com/olaplex-the-science-behind-the-strand/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2018, Olaplex won a patent infringement action against [[L'Oréal]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hopewel |first1=Bethan |last2=Fred |first2=Wu |title=Olaplex v L'Oréal |url=https://www.intellectualpropertymagazine.com/legal_updates/olaplex-v-loreal-130682.htm |website=Intellectual Property Magazine |publisher=Maritime Intelligence |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044555/https://www.intellectualpropertymagazine.com/legal_updates/olaplex-v-loreal-130682.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2015, Hawker was named as an [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] fellow for "revolutionising materials research through the development of powerful synthetic methods and strategies for molecularly engineering functional macromolecules, inspiring scientists across multiple disciplines."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sonia |first1=Frenandez |title=Materials Professor at UCSB Craig Hawker Named AAAS Fellow |url=https://www.noozhawk.com/article/materials_professor_at_ucsb_craig_hawker_named_aaas_fellow |website=Noozhawk |date=30 November 2015 |publisher=Local Independent Online News (LION) Publishers. |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044653/https://www.noozhawk.com/article/materials_professor_at_ucsb_craig_hawker_named_aaas_fellow |url-status=live }}</ref> He also serves or has served as editor for journals, such as the ''Journal of Polymer Science'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Craig Hawker |url=http://www.cns.ucsb.edu/people/craig-hawker-0.html |publisher=Center for Nanotechnology in Society |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044230/http://www.cns.ucsb.edu/people/craig-hawker-0.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and is on the editorial board for a number of journals of chemistry, including the ''International Journal of Polymeric Materials'',<ref>{{cite journal |title=Editorial Board EOV |journal = International Journal of Polymeric Materials and Polymeric Biomaterials|volume = 63|issue = 18|pages = ebi|publisher=Taylor & Francis Online |doi = 10.1080/00914037.2015.943833|year = 2014|s2cid = 216559276}}</ref> and the ''[[Journal of Polymer Science Part A]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Journal of Polymer Science Editor Craig Hawker Elected to Royal Society |url=https://www.wiley.com/WileyCDA/Section/id-405974.html |publisher=Wiley |access-date=26 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044710/https://www.wiley.com/WileyCDA/Section/id-405974.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2017, Hawker was described as "one of the top materials scientists in the world, "<ref>{{cite web |last1=Adela |first1=Talbot |title=Governor General taps trio for top PhD honours |url=https://news.westernu.ca/2017/10/governor-general-taps-trio-top-phd-honours-2/ |website=Western News |date=26 October 2017 |publisher=Western University |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306043756/https://news.westernu.ca/2017/10/governor-general-taps-trio-top-phd-honours-2/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2018, he and his colleagues developed a "3D-printing technique that can produce objects with both rigid and flexible properties will allow scientists to make bioinspired structures in just a single stage."<ref>{{cite journal |title=Lighting the way to versatile 3D printing |journal=Nature |year=2018 |volume=559 |issue=7713 |page=155 |doi=10.1038/d41586-018-05629-5 |pmid=29991780 |bibcode=2018Natur.559S.155. |s2cid=51612869 |doi-access=free }}</ref> This could lead to the development of structures with "mechanically and chemically distinct properties". Hawker is researching nanostructured materials in areas associated with [[microelectronics]] and [[biotechnology]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Craig J. Hawker |url=http://bpc2018.u-bordeaux.fr/en/Speakers/Plenary-speakers/Professor-Craig-J-HAWKER-i1648.html |website=Bordeaux Polymer Conference – May 28–31, 2018 |publisher=Bordeaux Polymer Conference |access-date=24 February 2019 |archive-date=24 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190224025338/http://bpc2018.u-bordeaux.fr/en/Speakers/Plenary-speakers/Professor-Craig-J-HAWKER-i1648.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
